title: Bhuvan Bam Interacts With 900 Students at Under25 Summit At Campus in BNMIT, Bengaluru
summary: Creator-turned-actor Bhuvan Bam spoke to around 900 students about creativity and evolving as an artist at Under25’s student-run Summit At Campus at BNMIT, Bengaluru.
body_html:
Bengaluru, 5 November 2026: Under25, the youth network, hosted its Summit At Campus (SAC) at BNMIT, Bengaluru, bringing together around 900 students for an on-campus cultural and edutainment experience. The highlight of the day was creator-turned-actor Bhuvan Bam, who interacted with students, performed on stage and shared insights from his journey.

During the session, Bhuvan spoke about his latest project, Dhindora S2, and reflected on his move from YouTube to larger entertainment platforms. He said every phase of a creator’s journey has its own time and opportunities, and that spontaneous ideas and improvisation often shape his work. Acknowledging YouTube for the platform, audience and opportunities that built his career, he also stressed the importance of evolving, experimenting and exploring new formats as an artist.

Encouraging students to trust their creative instincts, he said, “If you are a creator and call yourself an artist, you aren’t dependent on any single platform. Aap kahin bhi jaake bawaal macha sakte ho.” In another notable moment, he said he dislikes referring to his audience as fans: “First of all, I hate this word - fans. These are all my friends.” He added that celebrities and creators should remain accessible to the people who consume their content.

Speaking about his return to the event, Bhuvan Bam said, “It feels amazing to be back at Under25’s Summit At Campus. I’m over 25 now but I miss this energy in my life. Young people have such zest to explore and go out there to whatever interests take hold over them. And organising events like the SAC gives them the opportunity to do so across arts and music, as well as entrepreneurship. That’s how I am where I am - it was only because I was encouraged to take part in extracurriculars like singing, that I am here today. I can’t wait to be back for another one!”

Jeel Gandhi, CEO, Under25, said, “Today’s generation doesn’t want to be defined by any one conventional archetype. They want to explore multiple areas that interest them deeply and are very future-focused. Having someone as multifaceted as Bhuvan Bam, alongside creators like Sharanya, Harmanpreet, Abhinay, and Poorav, who cut across diverse creative fields like comedy, music or fitness, reflected this attitude perfectly.” He added that the summit gave students a glimpse of the many paths available to them and the confidence to create their own.

The day blended conversations, performances and student-led segments reflecting youth culture and expression. The line-up also featured creators Sharanya, Poorav, Harman and Abhinay.

Summits At Campus are licensed and entirely student-run through Under25’s nationwide fellowship network, giving students hands-on experience in programming, partnerships and leadership. According to the organisers, Under25 has held over 200 summits across 36 cities, reaching more than 1.2 million students, with the Bengaluru edition adding to that work.
